scenario.prompt_to_agent:
The TPO terminal (192.168.3.5) reports they cannot reach any
Internet Lab PC (128.168.0.x). At the same time, every PC in
the IT Department and CS Department reports they cannot reach
ANYTHING outside their own department. The Principle Room and
Other zone can still reach the Server Room and Internet Lab
normally. Find what broke.

injection.action: bring down the WAN-side link to router0

pre_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router1's Serial2/0 (eth2) interface, the
  10.10.0.0/8 link between router0 and router1
Mechanism: router0 is the gateway for IT (192.168.1.0/24)
  and CS (192.168.2.0/24). It only reaches the rest of the
  network (router1, router2, all their attached subnets) via
  the Serial link to router1. With that link down, RIP on
  router1 ages out 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24, and
  router0 ages out everything else. The TPO->128.168.0.2
  path is router1 -> router2 -> Switch5, which does NOT
  cross the down link, so it stays up.
Localization: router1 eth2 (or router0 eth2 — both ends of
  the 10.10.0.0/8 link)
Root cause: WAN link router0<->router1 (10.10.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth2 up` on router1 (or router0 if that side
  is down)
scoring_axes: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is router1's eth2 interface being operationally down. eth2 is the
WAN port on the wan_r0_r1 segment (IP 10.10.0.2/8) that connects router1 to
router0. Although the IP address is configured, the interface is in Linux
state DOWN (flags show <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> without UP,LOWER_UP), meaning it
neither sends nor receives frames.

This breaks the RIP adjacency between router0 and router1 entirely. Because
router1's eth2 is down, router1 never advertises routes for the IT
(192.168.1.0/24) or CS (192.168.2.0/24) subnets into the wider RIP domain,
and router0 cannot learn or re-learn routes to any segment beyond itself. On
startup, router0 briefly held stale RIP-learned routes (to 192.168.3.0/24,
192.168.4.0/24, 128.168.0.0/16, etc.) propagated when eth2 came up transiently
during container boot, but after the 180-second RIP timeout, those routes aged
out. Router0's table is now stripped to its three directly connected subnets
only, so every packet from IT or CS hosts hits router0 and is immediately
rejected with ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" — explaining the complete IT/CS
isolation. The TPO complaint was a transient convergence symptom: during the
brief window while router0's stale routes were expiring, return paths were
intermittently broken, but the router1↔router2 path (eth3, 20.20.0.0/8) was
never affected, and TPO→Internet connectivity is now confirmed functional.

Root cause: router1's eth2 interface was brought down (ip link set eth2 down),
severing the WAN link to router0 and collapsing the RIP adjacency on that
segment.

Corrective fix: On router1, run `ip link set eth2 up`. This restores the
Layer-2 path over wan_r0_r1; RIP will re-form the adjacency within one update
interval (≤30 s) and router0 will re-learn all remote routes, restoring full
connectivity for IT and CS departments.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names router1 eth2 on the wan_r0_r1 segment (10.10.0.2/8) connecting router1 to router0, identifying the router0–router1 10.10.0.0/8 link as affected.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only IT/CS are affected, not Other/Principle
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly states IT and CS are isolated while other paths (e.g., router1→router2, TPO→Internet) remain up, distinguishing the affected symptom pattern correctly.
States to run `ip link set eth2 up` on router1, which matches the expected corrective action.

The agent's investigation logs contain direct observations (router1 eth2 down, ping failures with ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' from router0, TPO→Internet reachable, router0's RIP-learned routes gone) that support the conclusion.
